title: Fast passback - Ariane Morales (runtime architect) — raw thoughts
content:
Quick context: met Ariane for a ~75m loop (onsite-style format over Zoom). Role we're hiring for: Senior/Staff Runtime Architect (focus: KV cache, routing, quantization tradeoffs). This is a raw memory dump — bias toward speed over polish. Use for sync with Marcus/Jordan before formal scorecard.

Overall impression (top-line):
- Smart system thinker, strong mental model for pipeline-level tradeoffs.
- Hands-on with low-level optimizations (has benchmarked kernel-level changes in past roles).
- Communication: concise, asked clarifying Qs early, used sketches to explain ideas.
- Risk: less experience with product-facing rollouts/CS interactions (weaker anecdotes on stakeholder management).

Candidate timeline / background notes:
- Senior eng (8+ yrs), last 4 yrs on inference infra at mid-size ML company (private).
- Implemented a custom KV cache eviction policy (LFU++ with time-decay) and shipped it to prod; claims 18% token-cost reduction on long-tail sessions.
- Past exposure to Triton and custom CUDA kernels; comfortable with PyTorch backends.

Highlights from technical deep-dive:
1) KV cache eviction design exercise (whiteboard):
   - Problem framing: candidate emphasized tail latency preservation and memory budget adherence. Good to see explicit SLO->budget mapping.
   - Proposed approach: segmented LFU with adaptive window + heuristics for prefix reuse detection.
   - Thoughtful on workload patterns: distinguished few-hot clients vs many-short.
   - Missing: concrete algorithmic complexity discussion (how to keep eviction decision O(1) amortized under high QPS). I had to press for implementation-level details.

2) Batching and compilation tradeoffs:
   - Clear on when to favor micro-batching vs synchronous small-batch: used examples with variable seq-length distributions.
   - Quantization: good practical sense (8-bit vs 4-bit), discussed accuracy regression monitoring and fallback strategies.
   - Mentioned integration with kernel-selection layer (our compilation piece) and how they would expose runtime telemetry for automated policy. Nice product-aware framing.

3) Live debugging exercise (trace triage):
   - Given synthetic trace with perf regression after model bump. Candidate enumerated hypotheses quickly (KV cache eviction pressure, kernel mismatch, GC on host).
   - Steps to validate: metric checks, repro, controlled rollback. Good pragmatic orientation.

Strengths (concrete):
- Strong systems intuition: can move from high-level SLOs to implementation levers quickly.
- Practical: knows common pitfalls (OOMs from kv cache growth, padding inefficiencies, tail latency causes).
- Familiarity with bundling telemetry -> automatable policies (what we want for Redwood Optimize).

Concerns / areas to probe further:
- Leadership + cross-org: examples of driving product tradeoffs with PM/Sales were shallow. Needs stronger stories about shipping with ambiguity across teams.
- Complexity management: proposed a few complex heuristics; would like to see simpler fallback-first approaches and explicit plan for operational burden.

Behavioral signals:
- Curious, asked good questions about our routing/fallback systems.
- Responded well to pushback; adapted plan after I suggested production constraints.

Immediate score (raw):
- Technical fit: 8/10
- Product/PM engagement: 5.5/10
- Communication & hiring bar: 7/10
- Overall leaning: strong technical hire, would prefer staff+ if we want an individual contributor with deep infra chops; borderline for manager-level role.

Recommended next steps:
- Give a short take-home focused on implementation details (not a long HW): ask for a 2–3 page design + pseudocode for a memory-bounded KV cache that supports prefix reuse detection and O(1) approximate eviction decisions; include a short test plan and metrics to observe in production. Limit: 4–6 hrs.
- Marcus to follow up on specific kernel/benchmark examples (we want to verify low-level CUDA/throughput experience).
- If take-home passes, invite to a small cross-functional session with PM (Priya) to assess product-level tradeoffs and stakeholder handling.

Notes for take-home rubric (quick):
- Correctness of basic design and rationale (30%)
- Operational simplicity / fallbacks (25%)
- Bench test plan and telemetry requirements (20%)
- Clarity of pseudocode and computational complexity (15%)
- Short answers on stakeholder tradeoffs (10%)

Unresolved questions to capture in Slack (send to #recruiting and #runtime-hiring):
- Can Ariane point to a specific PR/repo where they implemented an eviction algorithm? (ask Marcus to request link)
- How many people did they directly mentor/lead in last role? (to judge potential for people management)
- Confirmation of hands-on CUDA kernel work vs coordination with infra team.

Small housekeeping:
- Candidate timezone: CET (good overlap).
- Compensation expectations: mid-staff band (cited current comp + equity range that is in budget).

Raw quotes/phrases I liked:
- "I measure any cache strategy by the wall-clock tail percentiles first."
- "If a heuristic adds operational toil, it loses by default unless it buys significant cost/latency wins."

Action items (short):
- [ ] Post this doc to candidate thread and tag Marcus/Jordan (Asha).
- [ ] Marcus: request PR link / micro-benchmarks.
- [ ] Jordan: draft take-home assignment using the rubric above (deadline Thu).
- [ ] If take-home ok -> schedule PM session next week.

End of notes. Use as internal fast-passback only — will formalize into scorecard if we move forward.
